results.title: Sequential retry with same key replays completed result
results.expected_by_claim: effects=1 (README: 'A retry with the same key replays result')

results.title: Concurrent same-process same-key calls (Layer-1 in-flight map)
results.expected_by_claim: effects=1 (README: 'The second caller awaits the first caller's promise')
results.notes: Their headline differentiator vs 'naive single-layer store'.

results.title: Lost response after commit: executor commits effect, then throws; retry with same key
results.expected_by_claim: effects=1 (headline: 'retries never fire side effects twice'; 'Exactly-once execution')
results.notes: failures NOT cached by design; store has no delivery_uncertain state, so an executor that committed at the provider and then threw is indistinguishable from a pure failure. Retry re-dispatches -> second side effect. F2/A10 class.

results.title: Crash after commit: pending row left by dead process, new process takes over
results.expected_by_claim: headline 'retries never fire side effects twice'; README sells re-run as 'crash recovery' without an uncertain-outcome state
results.notes: reset() overwrites pending unconditionally (memory.ts:60-71; postgres.ts:72-77) — no liveness proof, no delivery_uncertain. Caller cannot distinguish 'recovered a crash before effect' from 're-executed after effect'. At-least-once in the ambiguous window.

results.title: Cross-instance concurrent race: two stores, one shared backend, winner mid-flight
results.expected_by_claim: effects=1 (README: 'only one caller ever wins the claim'; 'exactly-once across restarts'; PostgresBackend is the shipped multi-instance answer)
results.notes: runOnce (store.ts:96-102): claim loser checks 'completed' only, then reset()s the ALIVE winner's pending row unconditionally and re-runs its own executor. Layer-1 map is per-process and cannot see the other instance. A10b twin (race of first calls).

results.title: Same key, different request payload (key collision semantics)
results.expected_by_claim: OBSERVED probe — README stores request meta but never compares it; Stripe-class APIs reject mismatches
results.observed: effects=1, r1={"chargedFor":"order-123","cents":4999}, r2={"chargedFor":"order-123","cents":4999} (replayed order-123 response for an order-999 request)
results.notes: claim() persists meta.request (store.ts:89-93) but no code path ever compares it. A buggy agent reusing a key across different orders silently gets the first order's result. Not a double-charge; a wrong-result hazard. Hardening suggestion, not headline.

results.title: Re-execute after TTL expiry (ttlMs=50)
results.expected_by_claim: OBSERVED probe — documented scope: replay window = TTL (default 24h)
results.notes: 'Exactly-once' is TTL-scoped by design (options.ttlMs, DEFAULT_TTL_MS 24h). Documented and coherent; recorded to bound the claim's coverage.
